newsitem.title: NORWAY: Oslo shares recover from early fall, outlook rocky.
newsitem.headline: Oslo shares recover from early fall, outlook rocky.

text.p: Norwegian shares clawed back from a sharp drop at the open on Thursday, but dealers said the outlook continued uncertain.

The financial sector remain the focus of attention as speculation mounted over the proposed merger between Christiania Bank og Kreditakasse and insurer Storebrand, and the market saw high turnover in the insurance group's stock.
Oslo's Total share index recover in afternoon trade to close just 0.13 percent down at 1,032.91 points after tumbling to an early low at 1,022.29. Turnover was 1.18 billion crowns.
Dealers said a threat of strike action by Norway's major union and due U.S. and domestic economic data, were adding to investors' nervousness.
"I think the worse has past for now in terms of a downside, but April will be rocky," said one dealer.

Trade in Storebrand accounted for 289 million crowns as speculation heated up over the intentions of billionaire Kjell Inge Roekke, who raised his stake in Storebrand to 10 percent, making him one of the largest shareholders along with Tiger Management Corp and Orkla.
